Florida Southeast Connection mainline at milepost 77.2, Okeechobee County
Okeechobee Clean Energy Center, Okeechobee County
No route map staged. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission order places the start at milepost 77.2 of the mainline along U.S. Highway 441 and the end at the Okeechobee Clean Energy Center.

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issued a certificate for this lateral on May 30, 2018, in docket CP17-463. Florida Southeast Connection filed its request on June 14, 2017. The order describes about 5.2 miles of 20 inch pipe starting at milepost 77.2 of the Florida Southeast Connection mainline and ending at Florida Power and Light's Okeechobee Clean Energy Center in Okeechobee County. It gives firm capacity of 400,000 dekatherms a day and an estimated cost of 30.1 million US dollars. A Federal Register notice from February 2018 gives the same length and diameter and states the capacity as 400 million cubic feet a day. Status is operating by inference. No notice that states the lateral's own in-service date was found. NextEra's 2019 annual report says the Okeechobee Clean Energy Center reached commercial operation on March 31, 2019, and the plant needs this lateral for its gas. The same report lists the Florida Southeast Connection system at 169 miles, and NextEra's pipelines page gives the same figure today. That matches the 126.3 mile mainline plus this lateral plus the 38 mile Riviera Beach Lateral. Start year 2019 is set from the plant start, and the month is left blank. The staged cost is the estimate at approval, not a final cost. This is a new segment of the Florida Southeast Connection Pipeline (P8161), which is unchanged.

Riviera Lateral; Martin-Riviera Lateral; MR-RV Lateral; RBEC Lateral
Martin Clean Energy Center, Martin County
Riviera Beach Next Generation Clean Energy Center, Palm Beach County
No route map staged. The line runs from the Martin plant along State Road 710 to the Riviera Beach plant in Martin and Palm Beach Counties, according to a pipeline surveyor's project page.

This is existing pipe that Florida Southeast Connection took over from Florida Power and Light. On March 9, 2018, Florida Southeast Connection applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, in docket CP18-108, to acquire about 38 miles of existing pipe, three compressors and related equipment in Martin and Palm Beach Counties. A Federal Register notice from March 28, 2018 gives a capacity of 384 million cubic feet a day. The commission approved the acquisition on August 6, 2018, according to its list of approved projects and a trade press brief. Florida Power and Light's 2018 report to the commission states that the sale closed on September 1, 2018, so 2018 and month 9 are staged as the start under Florida Southeast Connection. The pipe itself is older. Florida Power and Light proposed a pipeline of about 32 miles to its Riviera Beach plant in 2012, and a pipeline surveyor's project page describes a 32 mile, 24 inch line costing 150 million US dollars. The original in-service year and the true diameter were not found, because the sources disagree on length and size, so diameter and construction dates are left blank. No Federal Energy Regulatory Commission order text for the docket was reached, so the approval date rests on the commission's own list. Also known as the Riviera Lateral, the Martin-Riviera Lateral, and the MR-RV Lateral. This is a new segment of the Florida Southeast Connection Pipeline (P8161), which is unchanged.
